  1. Solve the linear equation. \[20=4(x+3)\]

  28. There are 3 extrema shown, so the minimum degree is 4.
  29. If \(b^2-4ac<0\), then two complex solutions. If \(b^2-4ac>0\), then two real solutions. If \(b^2-4ac=0\), then one real solution (with multiplicity 2).
  30. \((x+3)(x-4)\)
  31. When you divide \(x^3+5x^2+2x-8\) by \(x-2\) the result is \(x^2+7x+16+\frac{24}{x-2}\), so the remainder is 24. The remainder is not 0, so \(x-2\) is not a factor.
  32. The solution set is \(\{-4,-2\}\), meaning both \(x=-4\) and \(x=-2\) are valid solutions to the equation.
  33. The remainder theorem tells us that \(p(4)\) equals the remainder when \(p(x)\) is divided by \(x-4\). Look at the graph to find the point \((4,-3)\) on the curve, which tells us \(p(4)=-3\), so the remainder is -3.
